title: Women's groups march to Delhi Police HQ over alleged sexual assaults
seoTitle: Delhi women's groups march to police HQ

tea.why: Protesters marched to denounce alleged sexual and gender-based violence by police personnel against demonstrators.
tea.want: They demanded prosecution of accused police personnel, accountability, and the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner.
tea.changed: Oct 17, 2026: Women's groups marched to the Delhi Police headquarters to submit a memorandum regarding alleged assaults.

summary: On October 17, 2026, several women's and student organisations marched to the Delhi Police headquarters in New Delhi to protest against alleged sexual and gender-based violence by police personnel during earlier demonstrations against the Election Commission of India. Carrying placards and banners, the demonstrators gathered near Gurudwara Bangla Sahib before marching to the headquarters to submit a memorandum. They called for strict legal and disciplinary action against officers accused of harassing women, transgender, and non-binary protesters, and demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral irregularities. The march was organized by groups including the All India Democratic Women’s Association, National Federation of Indian Women, and several other associations.
demands: Prosecute police personnel accused of sexual assault and harassment
Hold guilty officers accountable under the law
Demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar
response: No official response reported in the sources regarding the march itself, though sources noted an ACP accused of sexual harassment claimed a journalist made casteist remarks against him, and a man was arrested for sharing a fabricated video.

updates.text: Women's groups and student organizations marched to the Delhi Police headquarters to submit a memorandum demanding accountability for alleged sexual assaults.
